purpose: Denormalize totalHours to User for leaderboard performance, add future-date validation for event creation, deprecate whyVoluntary in favor of whyVolunteer, replace console.log with winston, fix circular import (logger/env), remove Phase 2 comments, and consolidate imports. Migration at backend/prisma/migrations/20260621120000_add_user_total_hours_and_why_volunteer/migration.sql properly backfills existing data.
riskRationale: All changes are backward-compatible. The whyVoluntary→whyVolunteer migration uses dual-field acceptance. totalHours denormalization includes a backfill migration. CreateEventSchema/EventSchema split correctly distinguishes creation from update validation. No existing API contracts or DB schemas are broken.
breakingChanges: User.totalHours field added - requires Prisma migration
VolunteerProfile.totalHours now write-only (readers migrated to User.totalHours)

text: Well-structured PR addressing 15 audit findings with clean, focused changes. The event schema refactoring (CreateEventSchema vs EventSchema), circular import fix, and totalHours denormalization show good architectural judgment. The backfill migration exists and correctly copies VolunteerProfile.totalHours to User.totalHours. A few minor issues remain around duplicated time-comparison logic, deprecated-field writes, and stale type annotations — none blocking merge.

message: Breaking the circular dependency by using process.env directly instead of importing env.ts is minimal and effective.
Replacing as never with Parameters<typeof prisma.$on>[0] is a fully type-safe fix that carries the correct Prisma event type union.

Extracting addEventRefinements to share meeting-link and time-ordering validation between CreateEventSchema and EventSchema is clean and DRY. The 5-second grace period on future-date validation protects against clock drift.
All three totalHours write paths (markAttendance, approveAttendance, checkOut) already dual-write to both User.totalHours and VolunteerProfile.totalHours in the same transaction, preventing drift.
Well-designed deprecation pattern: logs a warning when the deprecated field is used, prefers whyVolunteer, with graceful fallback to whyVoluntary for existing clients.
Migration properly backfills User.totalHours from VolunteerProfile.totalHours and whyVolunteer from whyVoluntary before switching reads. Critical for correctness.
The @@index([points, totalHours]) compound index correctly covers the most common leaderboard sort (points desc).

Controller writes to the deprecated whyVoluntary field alongside whyVolunteer with the same value. This prevents eventual removal of the column — the deprecated field will never converge to empty/NULL because every registration populates it perpetually.
suggestion: Remove the whyVoluntary write (line 88) and only write to whyVolunteer. The deprecated field retains existing data but stops accumulating new writes, enabling a future cleanup migration.

message: EventSeriesSchema duplicates the HH:MM time-comparison logic from addEventRefinements (lines 86-93). Same minute-calculation (endH * 60 + endM > startH * 60 + startM) appears verbatim in both places, creating a maintenance risk.
suggestion: Extract the time comparison into a shared helper function and use it in both addEventRefinements and EventSeriesSchema.

message: BatchData.profile type declares totalHours: number but the actual prisma.volunteerProfile.findUnique query (line 62-65) only selects bio and currentStreak, not totalHours. At runtime, data.profile?.totalHours is undefined, not number — a type inaccuracy that could mask bugs.
suggestion: Remove totalHours from the BatchData.profile type since it is no longer fetched from VolunteerProfile.
suggestionCode: profile: { bio: string | null; currentStreak: number } | null;

message: addEventRefinements validates that virtual events have a meetingLink but does not validate that in-person events (isVirtual: false) should NOT have a meetingLink. A client could send meetingLink for an in-person event and it would be silently stored.
suggestion: Add a refinement that rejects or strips meetingLink when isVirtual is false, e.g. refine((data) => data.isVirtual || !data.meetingLink, { message: 'Meeting link should not be provided for in-person events', path: ['meetingLink'] })

message: VolunteerProfile.totalHours is now write-only dead schema. All reads have migrated to User.totalHours, but events.service.ts still performs dual writes (lines 450-457, 587-594, 791-798). This wastes DB storage and creates maintenance ambiguity about the canonical source of truth.
suggestion: Remove VolunteerProfile.totalHours from the schema in a follow-up migration after ensuring all write paths only write to User.totalHours.

message: The composite index @@index([points, totalHours]) optimizes points-sorted queries but does not help hours-sorted queries (orderBy: { totalHours: 'desc' }), which require a standalone index on totalHours.
suggestion: Add @@index([totalHours]) to the User model for optimal hours-based leaderboard queries.

message: The deprecation warning logs on every registration that uses whyVoluntary. During transition this creates log noise on every deprecated-field submission.
suggestion: Track deprecated-field usage in-memory and log the warning at most once per process restart, or use a reasonable sampling rate.

message: Test mock for prisma.volunteerProfile.findUnique still includes totalHours: 5 even though the badge engine no longer reads totalHours from volunteerProfile. This dead mock value is misleading.
suggestion: Remove totalHours from the volunteerProfile.findUnique mock data.

message: logger.ts reads process.env.NODE_ENV at module-evaluation time, before dotenv.config() runs in env.ts (imported after logger). If NODE_ENV is set only in .env, the logger initializes with the default 'development' format.
suggestion: Defer logger format initialization until first use, or re-read NODE_ENV lazily inside the format function instead of capturing it at module scope.

reasoning: All functional changes are correct, backward-compatible, and backed by a data migration. The backfill migration exists and properly copies existing VolunteerProfile.totalHours to User.totalHours. Remaining issues are minor (stale types, duplicated time-comparison logic, deprecated-field write, missing index) — all are follow-up items, not blockers. The two important issues (whyVoluntary write in controller, EventSeriesSchema duplication) are design choices that don't cause bugs.
